skill.name: arch-doc-generation
skill.description: Generate structured Markdown documents for software architecture, technical proposals, API design, and deployment architecture.
skill.summary: Turn system requirements and technical decisions into review-ready architecture documentation.

content.value_statement: Architecture decisions often remain scattered across requirements, discussions, and diagrams. This skill organizes them into consistent Markdown documents for implementation and review.
actual_capabilities: Creates architecture design documents with background, principles, modules, data, security, deployment, and nonfunctional requirements.
Structures technical proposals with technology choices, system flows, interfaces, implementation stages, and risk assessments.
Produces API design documents covering protocols, authentication, versioning, endpoints, examples, and error codes.
Documents deployment topology, availability, disaster recovery, monitoring, and alerting considerations.
Formats outputs in Markdown with headings, tables, placeholders, and architecture decision records.
limitations: It does not validate the proposed architecture against a running system or source code.
It does not create PDF files without a separate PDF generation skill.
It requires accurate requirements, constraints, and decisions to produce specific documentation.
It provides document structure but does not replace security, reliability, or compliance review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a system design review
use_cases.description: Convert project requirements and constraints into a structured architecture document for stakeholder review.

use_cases.title: Define a service API
use_cases.description: Document endpoint conventions, authentication, resources, request behavior, responses, and error handling.

use_cases.title: Plan a production deployment
use_cases.description: Describe topology, availability, recovery, observability, security controls, and operational risks before release.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic architecture outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Markdown architecture outline for {{system_name}}. Include background, scope, key modules, data storage, deployment, security, and open questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a project needs an initial documentation structure.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an API design document
prompt_templates.prompt: Write an API design document for {{service_name}}. Cover protocol, authentication, versioning, resources, endpoint behavior, pagination, errors, and example interactions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before API implementation or interface review.

prompt_templates.title: Develop a technical proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a technical proposal for {{initiative}} using these requirements: {{requirements}}. Compare options, explain decisions, map core flows, identify risks, and propose delivery stages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a team must evaluate implementation choices.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a complete architecture specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Produce a review-ready architecture specification for {{system_name}} using {{context}}. Include C4 descriptions, module contracts, data flows, deployment, security, reliability targets, tradeoffs, ADRs, and unresolved decisions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a detailed cross-team architecture review.

output_examples.input: Document the architecture for a multi-region order platform with strict availability requirements.
output_examples.output: A structured Markdown specification covering system context, service responsibilities, data ownership, regional failover, recovery objectives, monitoring, security, tradeoffs, and architecture decisions.

output_examples.input: Create an API design for an inventory reservation service.
output_examples.output: An API document defining authentication, resource models, reservation operations, idempotency, concurrency behavior, pagination, error handling, and representative request flows.

output_examples.input: Prepare a technical proposal for replacing scheduled synchronization with events.
output_examples.output: A proposal comparing synchronization approaches, selecting event-driven integration, describing topics and consumers, planning migration stages, and recording delivery risks.

best_practices: Provide business goals, scope, constraints, expected scale, and existing technology before requesting a document.
Separate confirmed decisions from assumptions, alternatives, and unresolved questions.
Review generated security, reliability, and operational claims with responsible specialists.
anti_patterns: Do not present placeholders or inferred details as approved architecture decisions.
Do not request a complete design without supplying system boundaries and measurable requirements.
Do not treat generated diagrams or examples as proof that an implementation meets its targets.

faq.question: Which document types can this skill create?
faq.answer: It supports architecture specifications, technical proposals, API design documents, and deployment architecture documents.

faq.question: What output format does it use?
faq.answer: It produces structured Markdown with headings, tables, placeholders, examples, and decision records.

faq.question: Can it generate a PDF?
faq.answer: No. Use a separate PDF generation skill after the Markdown content is complete.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide goals, scope, users, constraints, expected scale, current systems, technology preferences, and known decisions.

faq.question: Does it verify architecture feasibility?
faq.answer: No. Engineers must validate assumptions, capacity estimates, security controls, and operational procedures.

faq.question: Can it document an existing system?
faq.answer: Yes. Supply accurate module, interface, data, deployment, and operational details for the current system.
